The exact public CSV blob identities for GPT-4o-mini r1-r5 and GPT-4.1-mini r1 match the six blob identities persisted by the clean worker. This removes the earlier provenance ambiguity about what repeated-judge records were analyzed.

The public README describes a 100-item expert-annotated benchmark and reports GPT-4o-mini MAAE 6.07 (+/-0.08) as an aggregate paper result. That is consistent in scale with the worker's five-run mean MAE 6.074, but the README aggregate alone is not an independent replay of every worker statistic.

reproducibility_assessment.reason: Exact public CSVs and their blobs are sufficient for future deterministic rowwise recomputation. This audit verified the binding and inspected the implementation, but did not claim a fresh execution of every result/bootstrapped interval.

safe_to_use: The exact 100-item LAJ public corpus and six judge-run CSVs are correctly source-bound to the worker result.

Within this narrow corpus, repeated GPT-4o-mini calls and GPT-4.1-mini model-name heterogeneity show strongly correlated errors under the worker's <=5-point definition, so raw judge count/name diversity is not sufficient evidence of correction value.
Verifier routing should be evaluated against class-conditional residual utility/cost rather than inferred from model-name diversity alone, as a hypothesis supported by this narrow negative example.
